title: UN Secretary-General Guterres calls for the Gaza ceasefire to become permanent
body:
On Monday 5 October 2026, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza ahead of the third anniversary of the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack, AFP reported. He said: "It is time for the ceasefire to become permanent," and urged a political path to lasting peace across the whole region.

Guterres described the 2023 attack as abhorrent and acknowledged that it killed more than 1,200 Israelis and foreign nationals and took 251 hostages. He said Palestinians in Gaza had suffered massive loss of life, displacement and destruction, and that their suffering also demanded an end. He said the ceasefire announced by President Donald Trump in October 2025 had brought some relief but had not delivered lasting security or a credible path to peace.

AFP cited the Palestinian Health Ministry as saying more than 74,200 people had been killed in Israel's military campaign in Gaza, figures the UN considers reliable. The report noted that Israel controlled most of Gaza and said it would not withdraw its troops until Hamas's disarmament was verified, while Hamas favoured gradual disarmament rather than an immediate and unilateral surrender of its arsenal.
